# Erdős Problem 550 for all trees — the Chvátal lower-bound construction

Erdős Problem 550 concerns the Ramsey numbers `R(T, K_{m₁,…,m_k})` of trees `T`
versus complete multipartite graphs.  The classical anchor is **Chvátal's
theorem (1977)**: for every tree `T` on `n` vertices and every `m ≥ 1`,
`R(T, K_m) = (m-1)(n-1) + 1`.  The *lower bound* half of Chvátal's formula has a
beautiful self-contained construction that works for **every connected graph**,
not just trees, and for *every* `n ≥ 1` (no "sufficiently large" hypothesis):

Colour the complete graph on `(m-1)(n-1)` vertices by taking `m-1` disjoint red
cliques of size `n-1`.  The red graph is a disjoint union of cliques, so its
connected components all have `< n` vertices and it contains **no red copy of any
connected `n`-vertex graph** (in particular, no red tree on `n` vertices).  The
blue graph is the complete `(m-1)`-partite graph, whose clique number is `m-1`,
so it contains **no blue `K_m`**.  Hence `R(T, K_m) > (m-1)(n-1)`.

This file builds that construction from scratch over Mathlib and proves the
lower bound as a witnessed non-arrow statement, with **0 sorries**.

-- !-- Lab Notes -- !--
Hypothesis (Hypothesizer): The "sufficiently large `n`" hypothesis in the paper's
  main theorem is unnecessary for the *lower* bound; the disjoint-clique colouring
  certifies `R(T, K_m) ≥ (m-1)(n-1)+1` for every connected `T` and every `n ≥ 1`.
Experiment (Experimenter): Modelled the vertex set as `Fin (m-1) × Fin (n-1)`
  (first coordinate = which red clique / which blue part).  Blue = "different
  part"; Red = its complement = "same part, distinct".  Proved red reachability
  forces equality of the first coordinate (`red_reachable_eq_part`), hence any
  injective homomorphism out of a connected `n`-vertex graph lands inside one
  part of size `n-1` — impossible.  Blue cliques inject into the part index set,
  capping their size at `m-1`.
Analysis (Analyst): The only place the tree hypothesis is used is *connectivity*;
  the construction is sharper than the paper's statement because it never invokes
  any largeness threshold.  The failure mode of a naive direct "tree embedding"
  argument is that subgraph (not induced!) copies must be modelled by injective
  homomorphisms, which `Reachable.map` handles cleanly.
Critique (Critic): Edge cases `m = 1` and `n = 1` make `(m-1)(n-1) = 0`; the
  statement is then about the empty vertex set and is still meaningful (no copy /
  no clique vacuously), so we keep `1 ≤ m`, `1 ≤ n` only where genuinely needed.
Synthesis (PI): Packaged as `chvatal_lower_bound`, a single witnessed statement.
-/
import Mathlib

open SimpleGraph Finset

namespace Erdos550

/-- The vertex set of the Chvátal blow-up: `p` parts, each of size `q`.
The first coordinate records the part (= which red clique). -/
abbrev Blow (p q : ℕ) : Type := Fin p × Fin q

/-- The **blue** graph: the complete `p`-partite graph with parts of size `q`.
Two vertices are blue-adjacent iff they lie in different parts. -/
def blue (p q : ℕ) : SimpleGraph (Blow p q) where
  Adj a b := a.1 ≠ b.1
  symm := by intro a b h; exact fun h' => h h'.symm
  loopless := ⟨fun a h => h rfl⟩

/-- The **red** graph is the complement of the blue graph: two vertices are
red-adjacent iff they are distinct and lie in the *same* part. -/
abbrev red (p q : ℕ) : SimpleGraph (Blow p q) := (blue p q)ᶜ

@[simp] lemma red_adj {p q : ℕ} {a b : Blow p q} :
    (red p q).Adj a b ↔ a ≠ b ∧ a.1 = b.1 := by
  simp only [red, blue, SimpleGraph.compl_adj]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨hne, h⟩; exact ⟨hne, not_not.1 h⟩
  · rintro ⟨hne, h⟩; exact ⟨hne, fun h' => h' h⟩

/-- A red edge keeps the part (first coordinate) fixed. -/
lemma red_adj_eq_part {p q : ℕ} {a b : Blow p q} (h : (red p q).Adj a b) :
    a.1 = b.1 := (red_adj.1 h).2

/-- Red reachability forces the first coordinate to agree: red connected
components live inside a single part. -/
lemma red_reachable_eq_part {p q : ℕ} {a b : Blow p q}
    (h : (red p q).Reachable a b) : a.1 = b.1 := by
  obtain ⟨w⟩ := h
  induction w with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons hadj _ ih => exact (red_adj_eq_part hadj).trans ih

/-- A *copy* of `T` in `G` is an injective graph homomorphism `T →g G`
(i.e. a subgraph, not necessarily induced, isomorphic to `T`). -/
def IsCopy {τ V : Type*} (T : SimpleGraph τ) (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∃ f : T →g G, Function.Injective f

/-- **Red side.** The red blow-up graph contains no copy of any connected graph
on `n` vertices when the parts have size `q < n`.  In particular it contains no
red copy of an `n`-vertex tree. -/
theorem no_red_copy {p q : ℕ} {τ : Type*} [Fintype τ] (T : SimpleGraph τ)
    (hT : T.Connected) (hcard : q < Fintype.card τ) :
    ¬ IsCopy T (red p q) := by
  rintro ⟨f, hf⟩
  -- all images share the same first coordinate (T is connected, red preserves part)
  obtain ⟨v₀⟩ := hT.nonempty
  have hpart : ∀ v : τ, (f v).1 = (f v₀).1 := by
    intro v
    exact red_reachable_eq_part ((hT.preconnected v v₀).map f)
  -- hence `f` lands in the part `{x | x.1 = (f v₀).1}`, a set of size ≤ q
  have hsub : Set.range f ⊆ {x : Blow p q | x.1 = (f v₀).1} := by
    rintro _ ⟨v, rfl⟩; exact hpart v
  have hcard_range : Fintype.card τ ≤ q := by
    have hinj : Fintype.card τ = (Set.range f).toFinset.card := by
      rw [Set.toFinset_range, Finset.card_image_of_injective _ hf, Finset.card_univ]
    have hpartcard : {x : Blow p q | x.1 = (f v₀).1}.toFinset.card ≤ q := by
      classical
      have : {x : Blow p q | x.1 = (f v₀).1}.toFinset ⊆
          Finset.univ.image (fun y : Fin q => ((f v₀).1, y)) := by
        intro x hx
        simp only [Set.mem_toFinset, Set.mem_setOf_eq] at hx
        simp only [Finset.mem_image, Finset.mem_univ, true_and]
        exact ⟨x.2, by ext <;> simp [hx]⟩
      calc {x : Blow p q | x.1 = (f v₀).1}.toFinset.card
          ≤ (Finset.univ.image (fun y : Fin q => ((f v₀).1, y))).card :=
            Finset.card_le_card this
        _ ≤ (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin q)).card := Finset.card_image_le
        _ = q := by simp
    rw [hinj]
    refine le_trans (Finset.card_le_card ?_) hpartcard
    intro x hx
    simp only [Set.mem_toFinset] at hx ⊢
    exact hsub hx
  omega

/-- **Blue side.** The blue blow-up graph (complete `p`-partite) has clique
number `p`: it contains no clique of size `p + 1`, hence no `K_m` with `m > p`. -/
theorem blue_no_clique {p q : ℕ} {S : Finset (Blow p q)} {m : ℕ}
    (hm : p < m) (hS : (blue p q).IsNClique m S) : False := by
  -- the map `a ↦ a.1` is injective on a blue clique, so `|S| ≤ p`
  have hinj : Set.InjOn (fun a : Blow p q => a.1) S := by
    intro a ha b hb hab
    by_contra hne
    have : (blue p q).Adj a b := hS.1 ha hb (by simpa using hne)
    exact this hab
  have hcardle : S.card ≤ p := by
    have := Finset.card_le_card_of_injOn (fun a : Blow p q => a.1)
      (fun a _ => Finset.mem_univ _) hinj
    simpa using this.trans (by simp)
  rw [hS.2] at hcardle
  omega

/-- The blow-up has exactly `p * q` vertices. -/
@[simp] lemma blow_card (p q : ℕ) : Fintype.card (Blow p q) = p * q := by
  simp [Blow]

/-- **Chvátal lower bound (no largeness hypothesis).**
For every connected graph `T` on `n` vertices and every `m`, there is a red/blue
colouring of the complete graph on `(m-1)(n-1)` vertices with **no red copy of
`T`** and **no blue `K_m`**.  Equivalently, `R(T, K_m) > (m-1)(n-1)`, i.e.
`R(T, K_m) ≥ (m-1)(n-1) + 1`.  This holds for *all* `n ≥ 1`. -/
theorem chvatal_lower_bound {τ : Type*} [Fintype τ] (T : SimpleGraph τ)
    (hT : T.Connected) {m : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m) :
    ∃ (red' : SimpleGraph (Blow (m - 1) (Fintype.card τ - 1))),
      Fintype.card (Blow (m - 1) (Fintype.card τ - 1)) = (m - 1) * (Fintype.card τ - 1) ∧
      ¬ IsCopy T red' ∧
      ¬ ∃ S : Finset (Blow (m - 1) (Fintype.card τ - 1)), (red'ᶜ).IsNClique m S := by
  refine ⟨red (m - 1) (Fintype.card τ - 1), by simp, ?_, ?_⟩
  · -- no red copy of T: parts have size n-1 < n
    apply no_red_copy T hT
    have hn : 1 ≤ Fintype.card τ := Fintype.card_pos_iff.2 hT.nonempty
    omega
  · -- no blue (= complement of red) K_m
    rintro ⟨S, hS⟩
    have : (blue (m - 1) (Fintype.card τ - 1)).IsNClique m S := by
      simpa [red, compl_compl] using hS
    exact blue_no_clique (by omega) this

end Erdos550

# Clique number of complete multipartite graphs `K_{m₁,…,m_k}`

The second graph in the Ramsey number `R(T, K_{m₁,…,m_k})` of Erdős Problem 550
is the complete multipartite graph.  This file establishes the single structural
fact about that graph which drives the whole reduction: its **clique number is
exactly the number of parts `k`**, independent of the part sizes `m₁,…,m_k`.

We prove both directions:
* `completeMultipartite_no_clique_succ` — there is no `(k+1)`-clique;
* `completeMultipartite_exists_clique`  — there is a `k`-clique (parts nonempty).

We then record the arithmetic *tightness* of Erdős Problem 550's conjectured
reduction bound `R(T, K_{m₁,…,m_k}) ≤ (k-1)(R(T,K_{m₁,m₂})-1) + m₁` against the
Chvátal values: in the all-singletons regime (`m_i = 1`, so `K_{m₁,…,m_k} = K_k`
and `K_{m₁,m₂} = K_2`) the conjectured bound is met with **equality**, which is
precisely Chvátal's theorem `R(T,K_k) = (k-1)(n-1)+1`.

-- !-- Lab Notes -- !--
Hypothesis (Hypothesizer): `ω(K_{m₁,…,m_k}) = k` regardless of part sizes, and the
  conjectured reduction bound is *tight* (not merely an inequality) at the Chvátal
  values, so it cannot be improved in general.
Experiment (Experimenter): For the upper direction, the part-index map `⟨i,·⟩ ↦ i`
  is injective on any clique (two vertices in the same part are non-adjacent), so
  `|clique| ≤ k`.  For the lower direction, one representative per part is a clique.
  For tightness, substituting Chvátal's `R(T,K_m) = (m-1)(n-1)+1` collapses the
  conjectured RHS to the conjectured LHS by `ring`/`omega`.
Analysis (Analyst): The clique number being *size-independent* is exactly why the
  paper's bound depends on `k` and `m₁` but not on `m₂,…,m_k` (beyond `R(T,K_{m₁,m₂})`).
Critique (Critic): The lower direction genuinely needs nonempty parts; with an empty

import Mathlib

open SimpleGraph Finset

namespace Erdos550

variable {ι : Type*} (V : ι → Type*)

/-- In a complete multipartite graph, two vertices are adjacent iff they lie in
different parts (recorded by the first coordinate). -/
@[simp] lemma completeMultipartite_adj {a b : (i : ι) × V i} :
    (completeMultipartiteGraph V).Adj a b ↔ a.1 ≠ b.1 := Iff.rfl

/-- **Upper bound on the clique number.** A complete multipartite graph with `k`
parts has no clique of size `k + 1`: the part-index map is injective on any
clique. -/
theorem completeMultipartite_no_clique_succ [Fintype ι] {k : ℕ}
    (hk : Fintype.card ι = k) {S : Finset ((i : ι) × V i)}
    (hS : (completeMultipartiteGraph V).IsNClique (k + 1) S) : False := by
  classical
  have hinj : Set.InjOn (fun a : (i : ι) × V i => a.1) S := by
    intro a ha b hb hab
    by_contra hne
    exact hS.1 ha hb (by simpa using hne) hab

theorem red_isKStarFree {p q : ℕ} (hq : 1 ≤ q) :

      _ ≤ (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin q)).card := Finset.card_image_le
      _ = q := by simp
  have hmem : v ∈ (Finset.univ.filter (fun x : Blow p q => x.1 = v.1)) := by simp

concept.lean_guess: Adapt the paper's reduction by constructing, for each k ≥ 3, a family of connected d-regular graphs with α(G) = k and d ≥ n/2 whose conformability encodes exact clique-packing problems in K_{k+1}-free complements. For odd k, conformable color classes map to cliques of sizes 1,3,...,k in G̅; for even k, to cliques of sizes 1,3,...,k-1. The key challenge is designing gadgets that force the correct distribution of clique sizes in any conformable coloring, generalizing the triangle-packing enforcement at k=3. A reduction from exact cover by k-sets or k-clique packing in K_{k+1}-free graphs would establish hardness.

A proof would likely construct, for almost every n, admissible tuples a_i whose total excess is ((k - 1) / log 2 - o(1)) log n, while controlling all odd-prime valuation constraints by showing that the binary carry construction can be locally repaired at negligible logarithmic cost.
